description: Third-person-singular present agreement for daily-routine verbs (audit commit ad3641395), rule en-third-person-daily-go-eat-have. With a 'every day' habitual marker present, a He/She/It subject + base verb (go/eat/have) is conjugated (eat->eats, have->has, go->goes). expectedStatus/expectedCorrection are the VERIFIED output of correctWithTutorRules('en') on current main (captured from the live engine): whitespace normalized, first character capitalized, rule loop, terminal punctuation.
fp_risk_note: Low FP risk; the main hazard is rule overlap. The eat/have positives isolate this rule cleanly because eat/have are NOT in the step5-SVA verb set {go,make,work}. The 'go' branch is in practice preempted: en-step5-subject-verb-agreement runs earlier and rewrites 'He go ...' -> 'He goes ...' before this rule sees it (so 'He go every day' is attributed to step5-SVA, not this rule) — that is current intended behavior. Negatives stress: already-conjugated input ('She eats rice every day'), the missing habitual marker ('She eat rice' with no 'every day' -> rule abstains; recall gap, not a defect), and a first-person subject ('I eat ...') which is correct English and must not fire.

positive.notes: eat -> eats with 'every day' marker; She subject. eat is unique to this rule, so it isolates cleanly from step5-SVA.
have -> has with 'every day'; He subject.

negative.notes: Already correctly conjugated — must not double-conjugate.
No 'every day' habitual marker, so the rule abstains. Recall gap (it does not yet catch bare third-person SVA on eat/have), not a false positive.
First-person subject is correct English; the rule is He/She/It only.
FP guard (question, second person): 'you' is not He/She/It, so no conjugation; stays unchanged.
FP guard (question, no habitual marker): without 'every day' the rule abstains, so the 'does she eat' question stays unchanged.
